hints: Focus on how solubility changes down Group 2, hydroxides and sulfates trend in opposite directions.
Remember hydroxides get more soluble down the group, so magnesium hydroxide is much less soluble than strontium hydroxide.
Remember sulfates get less soluble down the group, so think about which sulfate is insoluble and which is very soluble.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two Group 2 solubility trends**

Think of this as two opposite patterns you must know. Hydroxides become more soluble down the group. Sulfates become less soluble down the group.

Trend summary:
$$\text{Solubility of M(OH)}_2: \text{Mg} < \text{Ca} < \text{Sr} < \text{Ba}$$
$$\text{Solubility of MSO}_4: \text{Mg} > \text{Ca} > \text{Sr} > \text{Ba}$$

**Decide what precipitates with NaOH**

Adding $\text{OH}^-$ ions can form $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ and $\text{Sr(OH)}_2$. The less soluble one reaches its solubility product first.

Precipitation reactions:
$$\text{Mg}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + 2\text{OH}^-(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{Mg(OH)}_2(\text{s})$$
$$\text{Sr}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + 2\text{OH}^-(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{Sr(OH)}_2(\text{s})$$
Since $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is less soluble, magnesium hydroxide is seen first.

**Decide what precipitates with H2SO4**

Adding $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ ions can form $\text{MgSO}_4$ and $\text{SrSO}_4$. Here the trend is reversed.

Precipitation reaction:
$$\text{Sr}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + \text{SO}_4^{2-}(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{SrSO}_4(\text{s})$$
$\text{MgSO}_4$ is very soluble and stays in solution, while $\text{SrSO}_4$ is sparingly soluble. So strontium sulfate is seen first.

options.A: Magnesium hydroxide is correct for NaOH, but magnesium sulfate is wrong for H2SO4. $\text{MgSO}_4$ is soluble, so it does not precipitate. This choice forgets that sulfate solubility decreases down the group.
options.B: Correct on both sides. $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is less soluble than $\text{Sr(OH)}_2$, so it precipitates first with NaOH. $\text{SrSO}_4$ is much less soluble than $\text{MgSO}_4$, so it precipitates first with H2SO4.
options.C: Both parts are reversed. Strontium hydroxide is more soluble, so it precipitates after magnesium hydroxide, not before. Magnesium sulfate is soluble, so it will not precipitate first.
options.D: Strontium sulfate is correct for H2SO4, but strontium hydroxide is wrong for NaOH. This choice applies the sulfate trend to hydroxides. Hydroxides become more soluble down the group, so $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ precipitates first.
